label: Mark 15:1
text: Immediately in the morning the chief priests, with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.

label: Mark 15:2
text:
Pilate asked him, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
He answered,
“So you say.”

label: Mark 15:3
text: The chief priests accused him of many things.

label: Mark 15:4
text: Pilate again asked him, “Have you no answer? See how many things they testify against you!”

label: Mark 15:5
text: But Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate marveled.

label: Mark 15:6
text: Now at the feast he used to release to them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.

label: Mark 15:7
text: There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.

label: Mark 15:8
text: The multitude, crying aloud, began to ask him to do as he always did for them.

label: Mark 15:9
text: Pilate answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”

label: Mark 15:10
text: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.

label: Mark 15:11
text: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should release Barabbas to them instead.

label: Mark 15:12
text: Pilate again asked them, “What then should I do to him whom you call the King of the Jews?”

label: Mark 15:13
text: They cried out again, “Crucify him!”

label: Mark 15:14
text:
Pilate said to them, “Why, what evil has he done?”
But they cried out exceedingly, “Crucify him!”

label: Mark 15:15
text: Pilate, wishing to please the multitude, released Barabbas to them, and handed over Jesus, when he had flogged him, to be crucified.

label: Mark 15:16
text: The soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they called together the whole cohort.

label: Mark 15:17
text: They clothed him with purple, and weaving a crown of thorns, they put it on him.

label: Mark 15:18
text: They began to salute him, “Hail, King of the Jews!”

label: Mark 15:19
text: They struck his head with a reed, and spat on him, and bowing their knees, did homage to him.

label: Mark 15:20
text: When they had mocked him, they took the purple off him, and put his own garments on him. They led him out to crucify him.

label: Mark 15:21
text: They compelled one passing by, coming from the country, Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go with them, that he might bear his cross.

label: Mark 15:22
text: They brought him to the place called Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, “The place of a skull.”

label: Mark 15:23
text: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he didn’t take it.

label: Mark 15:24
text: Crucifying him, they parted his garments among them, casting lots on them, what each should take.

label: Mark 15:25
text:
It was the third hour,
 and they crucified him.

label: Mark 15:26
text: The superscription of his accusation was written over him, “THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

label: Mark 15:27
text: With him they crucified two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.

label: Mark 15:28
text: The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, “He was counted with transgressors.”

variants.reading: the whole verse ('The Scripture was fulfilled, which says, "He was counted with transgressors."') is omitted
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Mark' records 'Verse omitted by aleph B C D Psi k syrs cop' for Mark 15:28. Sinaiticus and Vaticanus are manuscript nodes of this graph and therefore get no preserves edge for this verse; the WEB prints it.

label: Mark 15:29
text: Those who passed by blasphemed him, wagging their heads, and saying, “Ha! You who destroy the temple, and build it in three days,

label: Mark 15:30
text: save yourself, and come down from the cross!”

label: Mark 15:31
text: Likewise, also the chief priests mocking among themselves with the scribes said, “He saved others. He can’t save himself.

label: Mark 15:32
text:
Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe him.”
 Those who were crucified with him also insulted him.

label: Mark 15:33
text:
When the sixth hour
 had come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.

label: Mark 15:34
text:
At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying,
“Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?” which is, being interpreted,
“My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

variants.reading: egkatelipes me ('you forsake me', Matthew's 27:46 wording)
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists 'me egkatatelipes' for C P X Delta Theta Pi2 f1 f13 28 700 and the Byzantine text; none of those is a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is empty.

The fetched variants article lists 'oneidisas me' for (D) it (c, (i), (k)); D (Codex Bezae) is not a manuscript node of this graph, so attested_by is empty. The WEB reading egkatelipes me ('forsaken me') is carried by aleph (Sinaiticus) and B (Vaticanus), which also carry this verse.

label: Mark 15:35
text: Some of those who stood by, when they heard it, said, “Behold, he is calling Elijah.”

label: Mark 15:36
text: One ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Let him be. Let’s see whether Elijah comes to take him down.”

label: Mark 15:37
text: Jesus cried out with a loud voice, and gave up the spirit.

label: Mark 15:38
text: The veil of the temple was torn in two from the top to the bottom.

label: Mark 15:39
text: When the centurion, who stood by opposite him, saw that he cried out like this and breathed his last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

label: Mark 15:40
text: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;

variants.reading: Maria he Iakobou tou mikrou kai Iosetos meter ('Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses')
variants.note: The fetched variants article lists this word order for aleph(c2) B (Delta Theta 0184 f1 1542, l844 not graph nodes) against 'Maria he tou Iakobou tou mikrou kai Iose meteer' in A Gamma 700 1241 and the Byzantine text. The WEB follows the Alexandrian wording.

label: Mark 15:41
text: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and served him; and many other women who came up with him to Jerusalem.

label: Mark 15:42
text: When evening had now come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Sabbath,

label: Mark 15:43
text: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member who also himself was looking for God’s Kingdom, came. He boldly went in to Pilate, and asked for Jesus’ body.

label: Mark 15:44
text: Pilate marveled if he were already dead; and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether he had been dead long.

label: Mark 15:45
text: When he found out from the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

label: Mark 15:46
text: He bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been cut out of a rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

label: Mark 15:47
text: Mary Magdalene and Mary, the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.

label: Barabbas was bound with insurgents who committed murder
statement: There was one called Barabbas, bound with his fellow insurgents, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.

label: The soldiers clothed Jesus in a purple cloak
statement: The soldiers clothed him with purple (a purple cloak) inside the praetorium, before leading him out to crucify him.

label: Simon of Cyrene was the father of Alexander and Rufus
statement: Simon of Cyrene, whom the soldiers compelled to carry the cross, was the father of Alexander and Rufus.

label: Wine mixed with myrrh offered at Golgotha
statement: They offered Jesus wine mixed with myrrh to drink at Golgotha, but he did not take it.

label: The crucifixion at the third hour
statement: It was the third hour (about nine in the morning, reckoned from sunrise) when they crucified him.

label: Isaiah 53:12 quoted at the crucifixion: 'He was counted with transgressors'
statement: At the crucifixion Mark 15:28 quotes the Scripture, 'He was counted with transgressors' (Isaiah 53:12) - a quotation in the text (reworded by reviewer 5 to neutral wording; the verse itself is absent from Sinaiticus, Vaticanus and other witnesses, recorded in the passage variants).

label: The ninth-hour cry 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani'
statement: At the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, 'Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?' - 'My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?' (Psalm 22:1 in Aramaic).

label: The watching women named: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James the less and Joses, Salome
statement: Women watched the crucifixion from afar: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome, who had followed and served him in Galilee.

label: The burial on Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath
statement: When evening had come it was the Preparation Day (paraskeue), that is, the day before the Sabbath.

label: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent council member (bouleutes)
statement: Joseph of Arimathaea, a prominent council member (bouleutes) who was also looking for God's Kingdom, boldly went in to Pilate and asked for Jesus' body.

label: Pilate verified the death with the centurion and granted the body
statement: Pilate marveled that Jesus was already dead, summoned the centurion, asked him whether he had been dead long, and on learning it granted the body to Joseph.
